executiveSummary.lead: The hotel reaches all 21 eligible scenarios and leads its certified four-hotel peer set, but appears in 78.6% of comparable answers and has only 28.6% Reality Coverage. The immediate task is to reconcile explicit first-party facts with the staged reality gaps, while treating technical-probe results as bounded observations rather than causal proof.

themes.title: Reconcile Official Dining Facts With the 0% Recognition Gap
themes.what: The official homepage describes multiple waterview restaurants and bars, including poolside, oceanfront, dockside, and tropical-bar experiences; the certified ADP read recorded 0% recognition for On-Site Restaurant.
themes.whyItMatters: The gap is commercially material because dining is explicit first-party content, but it does not prove that page copy caused measured AI performance.

themes.title: Strengthen the Resort, Beach, and Cottage Fact Architecture
themes.what: The official homepage states that the property is a Bermuda luxury resort with cottage accommodations, four private beaches, and two private coves. The staged reality-gap read recorded 0% for Luxury Positioning, Resort Experience, and Outdoor Pool, and 1.2% for Island Resort.
themes.whyItMatters: These are defining product facts. Consistent, approved presentation can improve decision context without promising a ranking, booking, ADR, or revenue outcome.

themes.title: Validate the Business-District Attribute Before Acting
themes.what: The staged review marks Business District Location as the first actionable 0% gap, while the certified property identity is an oceanfront resort in Sandys Parish.
themes.whyItMatters: A potentially inapplicable attribute should not trigger public copy changes until hotel leadership and the measurement steward confirm the intended demand context.
